name: Oholah
title: Samaria's Allegorical Sister
summary: Oholah is an allegorical figure in the book of Ezekiel representing Samaria, the capital of the Northern Kingdom (Israel). She is portrayed as an unfaithful woman who committed spiritual adultery by seeking alliances with Assyria and Egypt instead of trusting in God. Through this metaphor, the prophet Ezekiel condemns the idolatry and political infidelity of the Northern Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Oholah and Oholibah Introduced
keyEvents.description: Ezekiel presents two sisters, Oholah (Samaria) and Oholibah (Jerusalem), both of whom engaged in prostitution in Egypt during their youth. They represent the two kingdoms of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Oholah's Adultery with Assyria
keyEvents.description: Oholah (Samaria) was unfaithful to the Lord by seeking political and religious alliances with Assyria. She lusted after Assyrian warriors and officers and adopted their idolatry.

keyEvents.title: Oholah's Idolatry from Egypt
keyEvents.description: Oholah never abandoned her promiscuity from Egypt, which she had practiced in her youth. She continued to turn to pagan nations for support instead of turning to God.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on Oholah
keyEvents.description: God handed Oholah over into the hands of her lovers, the Assyrians, whom she had desired. They exposed her, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword—a prophetic description of Samaria's fall in 722 BC.

keyEvents.title: Oholah as a Warning to Oholibah
keyEvents.description: Despite the fact that Oholibah (Jerusalem) saw her sister Oholah's fate, she did not learn from it but became even more corrupt in her unfaithfulness. Oholah's downfall served as a warning which Jerusalem ignored.

keyEvents.title: The final judgment on both sisters
keyEvents.description: God declares that both sisters will be judged for their sins. Righteous men shall judge them according to the law for adultery and bloodshed, as a warning against idolatry and unfaithfulness to the Lord.
